en: So let's start with a bit of important
theory. What exactly is a VPS? Well, it
stands for Virtual Private Server,
and the idea behind a VPS is
that you typically have one machine, so one
computer
that is
somewhere in some data center by some
VPS compute provider like AWS, for example,
and that machine is then sliced up into
multiple
virtual
servers. So you have that one machine, but
in there you have multiple VPSs, multiple
virtual private servers. So you can think of
a VPS as a slice of an overall machine. Now,
when I say slice,
I mean strongly isolated. Of course. So each
VPS on that machine is isolated from the
other machines on it. So if you are renting
this VPS, let's say,
and your neighbor who may be owning this VPS
is doing something bad in their VPS and
crashes their machine or hacks their
machine,
it's just that VPS that is influenced by
that, not your VPS. Your VPS is fully
isolated from what's happening in those
other VPS machines, these other VPS servers.
That's the idea. So you,
in the end, own a slice of a machine, but to
you it feels like a standalone computer
because it works like a standalone computer.
Your VPS has its own operating system. You
can install any software you want on that
VPS, and it has its own dedicated resources
so that VPS, each slice here gets its own
slice of the overall available memory, of
the overall available CPU, and so on. So it
really is like a
computer, a standalone computer, just
technically it's part of a bigger machine.
The alternative to that, just to get that
out of the way too,
would be a
dedicated server where you rent an overall
machine. That is possible. Many providers
out there offer this feature or this
service, but of course, it's also typically
way more expensive because we're talking
about quite powerful machines with lots of
CPU cores, lots of memory, lots of
disk space,
and that of course will come at a certain
price point. That is why VPSs are so popular
because the provider can slice up the
overall machine in all kinds of VPSs.
So these slices don't have to be equal.
There may be some VPS
offerings here which offer more resources
and some which are cheaper and offer less
resources, less CPU cores and so on. And you
can pick exactly the one you need for your
project and then just pay for those
resources,
which is again why that VPS approach is so
popular.
